title: Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 3): Recovery hacks & supplements
summary: The last part of his patellar tendinitis guide covers everyday recovery: strict icing rules (gel packs, 15 minutes maximum, never mid-session or straight after leg training, twice on squat nights), morning knee extensions and bends, avoiding overextension stretches, wrapping rather than hole braces, and managing stress. For supplements he recommends MSM and turmeric; glucosamine and fish oil did little for him.
claims: He is not big on supplements for muscle, but for joint integrity and recovery they matter more
During rehab, leg training frequency should stay low: technique practice that tickles the tendon with blood without straining it
Icing is the key to healing patellar tendinitis; he avoids painkillers and anti-inflammatories
Use reusable gel ice packs with thin covers, never ice directly on skin or messy plastic-wrapped cubes
Icing reduces inflammation, and afterwards the body floods the area with nutrient- and oxygen-rich blood to rewarm it
Ice for 5 minutes at first, then 10, with 15 minutes as the maximum and never over 20; frozen tendons can be permanently damaged, as some NBA players found after falling asleep with ice on
Never ice during training or right before activity; after removing the pack, rest the knee as long as it was iced
The patellar tendon responds well to icing because it is exposed, unlike deep structures such as the ACL or MCL
Ice whenever you have downtime, up to five times a day, as long as you follow the rules
Do not ice straight after leg training; inflammation is the body's own response, so wait 2-3 hours; this is also why anti-inflammatories hinder healing
On squat days ice twice: e.g. train at 6 pm, ice at 9 pm and again right before bed
Each morning do knee extensions from a small range to full, not knee flexions, to clear stiffness, then repeated knee bends until the pain fades
Avoid full-body cat-style stretches that overextend the knee; stretch with the legs folded underneath you instead
Knee braces with a kneecap hole are useless for patellar tendinitis; wrap a band of fabric to stabilise the kneecap and wear it under clothes all day, as he did for months
Stress worsens tendinitis; you need a strong mind and a genuine desire to heal
MSM powder is cheap, horribly bitter and takes weeks to work, but is anti-inflammatory and reduces tendon pain; take about a teaspoon a day in juice, starting lower; he still takes it
Glucosamine costs more than MSM and he saw little difference from it
He put turmeric in every dish and drink while healing; absorption is debated, but he considers it great for health
Fish oil did nothing noticeable for him, so he stopped
Supplements are only supplements; healing requires actions and good habits
exercises: start with small range, extend further
clears morning stiffness, sends blood to tendon
start the day with blood in the knee
